title: Sales rise. Why might investment fall?
caption: Higher sales do not always mean more investment.
zh: 销售额上升，投资却可能下降。为什么？
speech: A factory sells more than ever. Yet its spending on new machines falls. How is that possible? The accelerator effect explains why changes in demand growth matter for investment.

title: A factory with eight machines
caption: Each machine produces 100 units per year at full capacity.
zh: 每台机器每年满负荷生产100件产品。
speech: Start with a factory producing eight hundred units a year, using eight machines at full capacity. Each machine produces one hundred units. Assume demand is sustained, productivity and machine prices are unchanged, and one machine wears out each year.

title: One purchase keeps the stock at eight
caption: 7 retained + 1 replacement = 8 operating machines
zh: 保留7台 + 替换1台 = 8台在用机器
speech: With demand unchanged, the factory replaces the worn out machine. Seven retained machines plus one replacement keep the operating stock at eight. Gross investment is one machine, but net investment is zero. Replacement maintains capacity; it does not expand it.

title: Demand rises from 800 to 1,000
caption: How many machines must the factory buy this year?
zh: 今年一共需要购买多少台机器？
speech: Now demand rises from eight hundred to one thousand units a year. The factory needs ten operating machines. Remember that one of its original eight wears out. How many machines must it buy? Pause and work it out.

title: Two additions require three purchases
caption: 7 retained + 1 replacement + 2 additions = 10 machines
zh: 保留7台 + 替换1台 + 新增2台 = 10台机器
speech: It buys three machines. One replaces the worn out machine, and two expand capacity. Net investment is two machines. Gross investment is three. Count this year's purchases, rather than all ten machines now in use.

title: Demand rises 25%; purchases rise 200%
caption: Unchanged machine prices: purchases and investment spending rise together.
zh: 机器价格不变：购买量与投资支出同比例上升。
speech: Demand rises by two hundred divided by eight hundred: twenty five percent. Annual purchases rise from one to three. That is an increase of two divided by one: two hundred percent. With unchanged prices, investment spending also rises two hundred percent. The small replacement baseline makes the percentage increase large.

title: The accelerator effect · 加速效应
caption: A change in demand growth can cause a larger percentage change in investment.
zh: 需求增长的变化，可能引起投资更大幅度的百分比变化。
speech: This is the accelerator effect. A change in the growth of demand can cause a larger percentage change in investment. Sustained demand growth raises the desired capital stock. Buying the extra capacity is induced investment: investment responding to changes in demand or income.

title: Faster growth requires more additions
caption: Year 3: demand rises by 600; net additions rise to 6 machines.
zh: 第3年：需求增加600件，需要新增6台机器。
speech: In year three, demand rises from one thousand to sixteen hundred. That needs six extra machines, plus one replacement. Gross purchases rise from three to seven. A larger annual increase in demand requires a larger addition to capacity.

title: Demand grows more slowly; investment falls
caption: Year 4: output rises to 1,800, but purchases fall from 7 to 3.
zh: 第4年：产量升至1800件，购买量却从7台降至3台。
speech: In year four, demand rises again, to eighteen hundred. But the increase is only two hundred, rather than six hundred. The factory needs two extra machines and one replacement. Purchases fall from seven to three, even though demand reaches a new high. Slower growth means less expansion.

title: No growth means no net additions
caption: Year 5: output stays at 1,800; one replacement is still purchased.
zh: 第5年：产量保持1800件；净投资为零，仍购买1台替换机器。
speech: In year five, demand stays at eighteen hundred. No extra capacity is needed. Net investment falls to zero, but gross investment remains positive because one machine still needs replacing. A high level of demand does not require repeated expansion.

title: Investment follows the change in output
caption: Compare annual output changes with annual additions to capital.
zh: 比较每年的产量增量与每年的资本增量。
speech: Read these two graphs together. Output rises, then becomes flat. Net investment follows the annual additions to output: zero, two, six, two, then zero machines. The key distinction is between the level of output and its change over the year.

title: The simple accelerator model
caption: I = v × ΔY: induced net investment responds to the annual output change.
zh: I为引致净投资；v为加速系数；ΔY为年度产量变化额。
speech: The simple accelerator model writes induced net investment as I equals v times the change in output. Here, v is a constant capital output ratio, and the desired capital stock adjusts fully. Delta Y is the absolute annual change in real output, not its level or percentage growth rate. Replacement investment is excluded.

title: A smaller increase in output
caption: v = 2. Output rises by £15bn, then by £5bn. Calculate I in each year.
zh: v = 2。产量先增加150亿英镑，再增加50亿。计算各年的引致净投资。
speech: Try this supporting calculation. The accelerator coefficient is two. Output rises by fifteen billion pounds this year, and by five billion next year. Calculate induced net investment in each year. Does investment rise or fall? Pause the video to answer.

title: Investment falls from £30bn to £10bn
caption: Output still rises; the addition to capacity becomes smaller.
zh: 产量仍然上升，但所需新增产能减少。
speech: This year, two times fifteen gives thirty billion pounds of induced investment. Next year, two times five gives ten billion. Investment falls by twenty billion pounds. Output still rises, but more slowly, so the required addition to capacity is smaller.

title: When is the accelerator stronger?
caption: Capacity, expectations and finance affect the response.
zh: 产能利用率、预期与融资条件影响投资反应。
speech: The response depends on conditions. When existing capacity is fully used and firms expect demand to last, expansion is more likely. With idle machines or a temporary rise in orders, firms may wait. Expensive borrowing or limited finance can also prevent the desired investment.

title: Multiplier and accelerator: two directions
caption: Multiplier: investment → income. Accelerator: income change → investment.
zh: 乘数：投资 → 收入；加速效应：收入变化 → 投资。
speech: Keep the direction clear. In the basic multiplier model, extra autonomous investment raises national income through spending rounds. In the accelerator, changes in income or demand induce investment. The two can interact, but they describe different causal relationships.

title: Equal annual increases in output
caption: Output rises by £10bn each year. What happens to induced net investment?
zh: 每年产量都增加100亿英镑。引致净投资会怎样变化？
speech: One final check. Output rises by ten billion pounds in each of three years. The accelerator coefficient stays constant and positive. Does induced net investment rise, remain constant and positive, or fall to zero? Choose before the answer appears.

title: The change in output drives investment
caption: Equal annual additions to output → equal positive induced investment.
zh: 每年产量增加额相同 → 引致净投资保持不变且为正。
speech: It remains constant and positive. Each year needs the same extra capacity. Remember three distinctions: capital stock versus investment flow; output level versus output change; and net investment versus gross investment. These explain why slower demand growth can reduce investment even while output is rising.
